title: Next-Generation Sequencing Assay for Somatic Mutation Detection in ctDNA
author: Heidi Fettke
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb3siqne
materials: Thaw plasma on ice. Extract cfDNA from plasma using the QIAamp circulating nucleic acid kit (Qiagen) as per the manufacturer's instructions. Elute into 50 µL buffer AVE. Pass the eluate over the column again to maximise yield after a second on-column incubation period of 00:01:00 . Note: Try to avoid extracting cfDNA from more than 6 patient samples at once in order to avoid cross-contamination as much as possible.

Assess size distribution, quality and quantity of resulting cfDNA using automated gel electrophoresis (2200 TapeStation and Expert software, Agilent) and the Qubit dsDNA high-sensitivity assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific). When using Qubit, it is a good idea to always use a control i.e. 1 µL of standard #2 Note: cfDNA can be stored at either 4 °C or -20 °C
Thaw buffy coat at room temperature. Extract germline DNA from buffy coat (containing peripheral blood mononuclear cells) using the QIAamp DNA blood mini kit (Qiagen) and elute into 200 µL buffer AE.
Quantify and qualify fragmented gDNA using automated gel electrophoresis (2200 TapeStation and Expert software, Agilent) and the Qubit dsDNA high-sensitivity assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Re-suspend library in 14 µL pure water
Variant not located in intergenic regions

Thaw plasma on ice. Extract cfDNA from plasma using the QIAamp circulating nucleic acid kit (Qiagen) as per the manufacturer's instructions. Elute into 50 µL buffer AVE. Pass the eluate over the column again to maximise yield after a second on-column incubation period of 00:01:00 . Note: Try to avoid extracting cfDNA from more than 6 patient samples at once in order to avoid cross-contamination as much as possible.

steps.title: Collect peripheral blood
steps.instruction: Draw whole blood into either an EDTA tube (process within 4 h) or a Streck Cell‑Free DNA BCT tube (if processing later), using a 21–23 G needle or larger; invert the tube ~5 times and avoid further agitation during transport.

steps.title: Initial plasma separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood tubes at 1900 × g, 4 °C for 10 min to separate plasma.

steps.title: Aliquot plasma and buffy coat
steps.instruction: Transfer plasma to 5 mL Eppendorf tubes without disturbing the buffy coat; collect the ~1 mL buffy coat layer into a cryovial and store both plasma and buffy coat at –80 °C.

steps.title: Clarify plasma
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plasma at 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min; transfer the supernatant to a fresh 5 mL tube, discard the pellet, re‑centrifuge to ensure no pellet remains, aliquot clarified plasma into cryovials and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Remove high‑MW DNA
steps.instruction: Treat the 50 µL plasma eluate with Ampure XP beads to eliminate large DNA fragments.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 µL Ampure XP beads (0.5:1 v/v) to the 50 µL eluate, incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic rack 2 min, discard supernatant (beads now contain DNA > 500 nt).
Add 50 µL Ampure XP beads (1:1 v/v) to the supernatant, incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Magnetically separate 2 min, discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol, discard ethanol each time.
Air‑dry beads 5–10 min (avoid over‑drying).
Elute cfDNA with 13 µL pure water, incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic rack, collect the eluate into a new tube.

steps.title: Shear gDNA
steps.instruction: Shear extracted genomic DNA to 150–200 bp using a Covaris ultrasonicator with settings: Duty Factor 10 %, Peak Incident Power 175, Cycles per Burst 200, Treatment Time 360 s, Bath temperature 4–8 °C.

steps.title: Prepare ThruPLEX libraries
steps.instruction: Use the ThruPLEX Tag‑seq kit (manufacturer’s protocol) to generate molecularly‑tagged libraries from cfDNA and gDNA, using 10–50 ng input (maximum 50 ng recommended).

steps.title: Library bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean library fragments with a 1:1 (v/v) ratio of Ampure XP beads, elute in 33 µL pure water, quantify with Qubit and verify size shift from ~170 bp to ~340 bp.

steps.title: Prepare SureSelect capture
steps.instruction: Set up Agilent SureSelect target enrichment using biotinylated RNA baits and four IDT blocking oligonucleotides (Thruplex p5‑UMI‑11nt, p5‑UMI‑8nt, p7‑UMI‑11nt, p7‑UMI‑8nt; ‘X’ denotes sample‑specific barcode/UMI).

steps.title: Hybrid‑capture first round
steps.instruction: Incubate libraries with baits for 24 h at 65 °C, applying the following modifications:

substeps.instruction: Replace SureSelect Block 3 with 0.5 µL of each indexing blocker plus 0.6 µL water (total blocking mix 7.6 µL).
Use 1 µL capture library instead of 2 µL (for libraries <3 Mb).
Perform four washes with 400 µL Wash Buffer 2, each incubated 20 min.
Resuspend the captured library in 14 µL pure water.

steps.title: PCR enrichment of capture
steps.instruction: Amplify the 14 µL captured library by PCR on a thermal cycler using the manufacturer’s conditions; number of cycles as specified in the kit protocol (not provided in the source).

steps.title: Post‑capture cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean the PCR‑enriched libraries with Ampure XP beads, elute in 33 µL pure water, quantify with Qubit, and store at 4 °C (up to 1 week) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: DCAP‑Seq repeat capture
steps.instruction: Repeat the hybridisation and PCR enrichment with altered conditions:

substeps.instruction: Incubate library with probes for 5 h at 65 °C (instead of 24 h).
Perform 5 PCR cycles (instead of 16).
Resuspend final libraries in 33 µL pure water.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Generate 50–70 million 100–150 bp paired‑end reads for cfDNA and ~1 million reads for gDNA on an Illumina HiSeq2500 in rapid mode.

steps.title: Demultiplex and align
steps.instruction: Demultiplex libraries using per‑sample indices, map reads to hg19 with BWA‑MEM v0.7.12, and convert to BAM files with Samtools v1.6.

steps.title: Error‑correct read families
steps.instruction: Use Connor v0.5 to group reads sharing identical molecular barcodes; require ≥3 replicates per family, consensus frequency ≥0.66, and retain only families meeting these criteria.

steps.title: Call somatic variants
steps.instruction: Run VarDict v1.5.8 in paired‑samples mode with standard filters, setting minimum variant frequency to 0.001 %.

steps.title: Filter VCF with VarSeq
steps.instruction: Apply the following VarSeq (Golden Helix) filters:

substeps.instruction: Somatic: status = ‘strong somatic’; exclude intergenic variants; retain loss‑of‑function or missense variants with CADD PHRED ≥ 20; exclude variants present in gnomAD Exomes v2.1.1 at >0.001 % frequency; minimum depth 500×; VAF ≥ 0.0025; ≥3 supporting reads; at least one forward and one reverse supporting read.
Germline: status = ‘germline’; minimum depth 8× in the germline sample.

steps.title: Manual IGV review
steps.instruction: Inspect all remaining variants in Integrative Genomics Viewer to remove sequencing artefacts or common variants missed by gnomAD filtering.

steps.title: CNV calling with VarSeq
steps.instruction: Generate copy‑number calls per sample using VarSeq CNV Caller with these settings:

substeps.instruction: Reference set: ≥30 germline BAMs sequenced with the same panel; pre‑deduplicated files preferred if post‑Connor depth is low.
Calculate coverage using the panel BED file.
Custom CNV parameters: maximum tumour‑reference difference 0.25, minimum target depth 50.
Deletion criteria: either (p‑value < 0.00001 AND ratio < 0.87) OR (p‑value < 0.05 AND z‑score < ‑0.85 AND ratio < 0.7).

steps.title: Conditional PCR enrichment
steps.instruction: If the library amount is ≤400 ng, perform 1–2 additional PCR enrichment cycles as described in step 12; otherwise proceed to downstream analysis.
